title: Too Much Coffee May Be Bad for Your Bones
paragraphs: Coffee is one of the most popular drinks in the world. However, a recent study suggests that drinking a lot of coffee may not be good for the bones of older women.

The study was published in the scientific journal Nutrients in late 2025. The researchers used data from a long-term study in the United States called the Study of Osteoporotic Fractures. It included 9,704 women aged 65 and older. Every few years, the women answered questions about how much coffee and tea they drank, and they had tests to measure the strength of their bones, which is called bone density. The researchers looked at about 10 years of data.

The results showed that drinking two to three cups of coffee a day did not seem to harm the women's bones. However, the researchers found that drinking five or more cups a day may be linked to lower bone density. The link between coffee and weaker bones also seemed stronger in women who drank more alcohol.

Tea, on the other hand, seemed to have a small positive effect. Women who drank tea had slightly stronger hip bones than women who did not drink tea. The benefit seemed bigger in women who were obese. However, the difference was very small, and it may not be important for individual people.
Why might too much coffee affect bones? According to one researcher, caffeine may make it harder for the body to absorb calcium, which is important for strong bones.

The study had some limitations. It was observational, so it cannot prove that coffee causes weaker bones. It also measured bone density, not broken bones. In addition, most of the women were white and lived in the United States, so the results may not apply to everyone.
